findings.title: Resource lookup uses wrong ownerId and fails to find client-specific resources
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (a UUID) as the `ownerId` parameter. However, when resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104: `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (via `RepresentationToModel`), the resource owner is set to `resourceServer.getClientId()`, or in JPA `server.getClientId()`. Using `server.getId()` may fail to match or is inconsistent with `AdminPermissionsSchema` which calls the 2-argument `resourceStore.findByName(resourceServer, name)` (which defaults ownerId to `resourceServer.getClientId()`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`.

findings.title: Created client resources do not have their resource type set in AdminPermissionsSchema
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String)` (line 138), resources are queried via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 104-111), when a resource for a specific client (or user) is created dynamically, `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the 'all-resources' resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has its type set. Because per-client resources have `type == null`, `findByType` will never return them, so `getClientsWithPermission` will miss all individual client permissions (and listing clients in `ClientsResource.getClients` will return an empty list when only per-client `view` permissions are granted, unless `canConfigure`/`canManage` happens to be evaluated via another path).

findings.title: All-clients permissions are ignored when a client-specific resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (lines 214-222), the fallback to the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ('all-clients') resource only happens when `resource == null` (i.e., no resource exists for that specific client). If a specific permission is created for Client A on one scope (e.g., `map-roles`), a `Resource` for Client A is created in the store. If another permission is granted on the 'all-clients' resource (e.g., `view` or `manage` all clients), `hasPermission(clientA, VIEW)` will find Client A's specific resource, evaluate only the policies attached to Client A's resource, and return `false` without ever evaluating the 'all-clients' resource policies (compare with `UserPermissionsV2`, which evaluates both the user resource and the all-users resource type).

findings.title: canView() does not return true when caller has MANAGE permission on all clients
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` (line 87) checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`, which does not check `canManage()` or `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. In contrast, `ClientPermissions.canView()` checks `canViewClientDefault() || canManage()`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel)` checks `canView() || canConfigure(client)` (which includes `canManage(client)`). As a result, an admin granted only the `MANAGE` scope on all clients will have `canManage() == true`, `canView(client) == true`, and `canView(clientScope) == true`, but `canView() == false`, causing endpoints that call `auth.clients().requireView()` or `canView()` (such as viewing clientscopes list via `canViewClientScopes()` / `canListClientScopes()`) to unexpectedly fail with 403 Forbidden.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only handles `USERS.getType()`, returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`. It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`. For client permissions, `resource.getDisplayName()` will be returned, which is `null` (or the internal UUID / `"Clients"`), instead of `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId` when policies/permissions are converted to representations for the Admin UI/REST API.

findings.title: Orphaned authorization resources and permissions are not cleaned up when a client or user is deleted in FGAP V2
findings.body: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (line 77), the `ProviderEventListener` for `ClientRemovedEvent` (and other removal events) is now gated behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (V1 only), and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Consequently, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled and a client (or user) is deleted from a realm, its corresponding `Resource` in the `admin-permissions` resource server and references to it in policies are never removed from the database. Worse, if a policy references that deleted client's resource, subsequent calls to `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (when implemented for clients, as it already is for users at line 318) will throw `ModelIllegalStateException` because the underlying entity no longer exists.
